title: Refraction through Prisms — 40 MCQs
description: The minimum deviation condition, the relation between the angle of the prism, the angle of minimum deviation and the refractive index, calculation of the refractive index of a prism, and deviation in a small-angle prism with its practical importance.

questions.q: For a prism, the angle of the prism A, the angle of incidence i, the angle of emergence e and the angle of deviation δ are related by
options: A + δ = i − e
A = i + e + δ
δ = i + e + A
A + δ = i + e
questions.explanation: In quadrilateral form the four angles give A + δ = i + e, so the deviation depends on the angles of incidence and emergence as well as on the angle of the prism.

questions.q: In the refraction of light through a prism, if r₁ and r₂ are the angles of refraction at the two faces, then
options: r₁ + r₂ = 2A
r₁ − r₂ = A
r₁ + r₂ = A
r₁ + r₂ = δ
questions.explanation: The two refracted rays inside the prism lie in a quadrilateral whose angles give r₁ + r₂ = A, the angle of the prism.

questions.q: At the position of minimum deviation, the path of the ray through a prism is such that
options: i = e and r₁ = r₂ = A
r₁ = A and r₂ = 0
i is much greater than e
i = e and r₁ = r₂ = A/2
questions.explanation: At minimum deviation the ray passes symmetrically through the prism, so the angles of incidence and emergence are equal and each angle of refraction is half the prism angle.

questions.q: The refractive index of the material of a prism, in terms of the angle of the prism A and the angle of minimum deviation δ_m, is given by
options: n = sin((A − δ_m)/2)/sin(A/2)
n = sin((A + δ_m)/2)/sin(A/2)
n = sin(A/2)/sin((A + δ_m)/2)
n = sin(A)/sin(δ_m)
questions.explanation: At minimum deviation i = (A + δ_m)/2 and r = A/2, so Snell's law gives n = sin((A + δ_m)/2)/sin(A/2).

questions.q: The angle of deviation produced by a prism is the angle between
options: the incident ray and the normal at the first face
the direction of the incident ray and the direction of the emergent ray
the two refracting faces of the prism
the emergent ray and the base of the prism
questions.explanation: The emergent ray is bent away from the original direction of the incident ray, and the angle between these two directions is the angle of deviation.

questions.q: For a thin prism of small refracting angle A and refractive index n, the angle of deviation is given by
options: δ = nA
questions.explanation: For a thin prism the angles are so small that Snell's law may be written in terms of the angles themselves, which gives δ = (n − 1)A.

questions.q: For a thin prism of a given material, the angle of deviation produced is
options: proportional to the square of the angle of the prism
inversely proportional to the angle of the prism
independent of the angle of the prism
directly proportional to the angle of the prism
questions.explanation: Since δ = (n − 1)A for a thin prism, the deviation is directly proportional to A and is independent of the angle of incidence.

questions.q: When light passes through a glass prism it is deviated towards the base because
options: total internal reflection occurs inside the prism
the two faces of the prism are parallel to each other
it bends away from the normal on entering and towards the normal on leaving
it bends towards the normal on entering and away from the normal on leaving, both refractions turning the ray towards the base
questions.explanation: Both refractions at the two inclined faces bend the ray in the same sense, i.e. towards the thicker part or base of the prism.

questions.q: As the angle of incidence on a prism is gradually increased from a small value, the angle of deviation
options: first decreases, becomes minimum, and then increases
remains constant at all angles of incidence
goes on decreasing throughout
goes on increasing throughout
questions.explanation: The i–δ curve of a prism is a curve with a single minimum, and the deviation is least when the ray passes symmetrically through the prism.

questions.q: The deviation produced by a prism depends on
options: only the angle of incidence
only the refractive index of the material
the angle of the prism, the refractive index of its material and the angle of incidence
only the angle of the prism
questions.explanation: Since δ = i + e − A, and e depends on i, A and n, the deviation is a function of all three of these quantities.

questions.q: In a prism experiment the angle of the prism is 60° and, at minimum deviation, the angle of incidence is found to be 48.6°. The angle of minimum deviation is
questions.explanation: At minimum deviation δ_m = 2i − A = 2 × 48.6° − 60° = 37.2°, which agrees with n = sin 48.6°/sin 30° ≈ 1.5.

questions.explanation: For a thin prism δ = (n − 1)A, so n = 1 + δ/A = 1 + 2/5 = 1.4.

questions.q: A ray of light is incident at 40° on a prism of angle 60° and refractive index 1.5 and suffers a deviation of about 38.5°. By the principle of reversibility of light, the same deviation occurs for an angle of incidence of
questions.explanation: Since δ = i + e − A, the deviation is unchanged if i and e are interchanged; here i + e = 60° + 38.5° = 98.5°, so when i = 40° the emergence angle is 58.5°, and the deviation is the same for i = 58.5°.

questions.q: For a thin prism the deviation is found to be almost independent of the angle of incidence because
options: the emergent ray is totally internally reflected
the ray passes through the prism without any refraction
the angles involved are so small that sin θ ≈ θ, so the deviation reduces to δ = (n − 1)A
the refractive index of the prism becomes equal to 1
questions.explanation: When i, e and A are all small, Snell's law gives the angles directly, and the deviation reduces to δ = (n − 1)A, which contains neither i nor e.

questions.q: Small-angle prisms are of great practical importance because they
options: produce total internal reflection for all angles of incidence
magnify distant objects by themselves
deviate a beam of light through a small controlled angle and are used in instruments such as prism binoculars and periscopes
disperse white light into a complete spectrum
questions.explanation: A thin prism of small angle gives a small, calculable deviation δ = (n − 1)A, and such prisms are used to turn beams through a fixed angle in optical instruments.

questions.q: For a ray of light to just emerge from the second face of a prism (grazing emergence), the angle of refraction r₂ at the second face must be equal to
options: zero
the angle of the prism A
the critical angle of the prism material with respect to air
half the angle of the prism A/2
questions.explanation: At grazing emergence the refracted ray at the second face leaves along the surface, so the angle of refraction there is 90° and r₂ equals the critical angle C = sin⁻¹(1/n).

questions.q: A ray of light is incident normally on one face of a prism of angle 30° and refractive index 1.5. The deviation produced is about
questions.explanation: For normal incidence i = 0 and r₁ = 0, so r₂ = A = 30°; then sin e = 1.5 sin 30° = 0.75 and e ≈ 48.6°. Hence δ = i + e − A = 0 + 48.6° − 30° ≈ 18.6°.
